decisions.description: The one router every save returns to. Each outcome is a follow-up that runs at most once (the WasVisited condition), in order: stamp the family's Household on the submission after Contact 1, make the person the Account's Primary Contact when their Primary Contact box is checked (or Contact 1 when the Organization has none), affiliate the person with the Organization, then chain Campaign Members; when nothing is left, return to the controller.

decisions.label: Switch

decisions.description: Joins the person to the Household already on the submission. Only a Household record (record type HH_Account) is ever written onto the Contact's Account; an organization is never a move in NPSP, it is an affiliation. Joining is asked for, not automatic: the template's Contact1 Add to Account rule on a Contact 1 pass, its Contact2 Add to Account rule on a Contact 2 pass, or the capturing section's own Add to Account setting. Without one of those, a household template still gives Contact 2 and repeater rows their own Household, which is what householdWithoutAddToAccount_contact2KeepsItsOwnHousehold pins.

decisions.label: Switch

rules.name: Join_Household
rules.conditionLogic: 1 AND 2 AND ((3 AND 4) OR (5 AND 6) OR 7)
rules.label: Join Household

Flow.description:
WHAT IT DOES: The one engine that saves every person in an NPSP form conversion: Contact 1, Contact 2, and every repeater or table row. The mapping steps decide WHAT goes on the Contact; this flow decides whether it is new or an existing person, saves it, puts it in the right NPSP Household, and logs the result. It follows the packaged Contact engine step for step, so anyone who knows that flow can read this one.
HOW IT WORKS, STEP BY STEP: 1. Blank form answers are stripped so they never erase data on a matched Contact, and the record type and owner are validated. 2. The Account on the submission (or on the parent submission for repeater and table rows) is read. When it is an NPSP Household and the template is in Household mode (its Account record type is HH_Account), or the Add to Account rule asks for it, the person joins that Household by setting the Contact's Account before the save. Only a Household is ever written onto a Contact. 3. The duplicate checker runs with the template's Contact matching rules; the single or most confident match is updated, otherwise the Contact is inserted through the bypass-duplicates action so subscriber Block rules and alerts cannot stop an unattended conversion. Several matches without Update Most Confident Match log an error: the pipeline refuses to guess. 4. The saved Contact is read back, because NPSP fills in the Household during the save. 5. The router runs each follow-up at most once. After Contact 1 in Household mode, the Contact's Household is stamped on the submission (a new Contact 1 gets one from NPSP, a returning one brings its own), so the Account rule updates it next and Contact 2 joins it. When the submission's Account is an Organization and the Add to Account rule for this contact (or the capturing section) asks for it: the person is affiliated with the Organization through the NPSP Upsert Affiliation utility. A person whose Primary Contact box is checked becomes the Account's Primary Contact (the Organization, or otherwise their Household); Contact 1 also fills a blank Organization Primary Contact when Contact 1's Add to Account rule is on. Campaign Members chain as in the packaged engine. Then it returns to the controller.
WHERE IT FITS: Installed through the NPSP Contact steps, which the Primary Contact and Alternate Contact records of Form Template Conversion Mapping Default point at. Organization links in NPSP are affiliations, never a change of the Contact's Account: only a Household is ever written onto a Contact.

recordLookups.description: Contact 1 may already sit under an Organization, and an Organization must never be stamped on the submission as the family's Household.
recordLookups.name: getContactAccountForStamp
recordLookups.label: Contact 1 Account (Stamp Check)

recordLookups.description: The Account this person could join: the submission's Account, or the parent submission's for repeater and table rows. Read so the next decision can check its record type - only an NPSP Household is ever written onto a Contact. Returns nothing when there is no Account yet, which is Contact 1's first pass.
recordLookups.name: getAccount
recordLookups.label: Account

recordLookups.description: Read back into the Contact variable: a save returns only the fields that were set, and NPSP fills in the Household (AccountId) during the save, so everything after this - the log and the Household stamp - needs the record as it now stands.
recordLookups.name: getContactInserted
recordLookups.label: Contact (Inserted)

recordLookups.description: Read back into the Contact variable: a save returns only the fields that were set, and NPSP fills in the Household (AccountId) during the save, so everything after this - the log and the Household stamp - needs the record as it now stands.
recordLookups.name: getContactUpdated
recordLookups.label: Contact (Updated)

recordUpdates.description: Names the person as the Account's Primary Contact (npe01__One2OneContact__c): the Organization when the submission's Account is one, otherwise the Household the person now belongs to. Runs when the person's Primary Contact box is checked (Contact 1 Primary Contact on the main submission, Contact 2 Primary Contact for Contact 2 and repeater or table rows), or for Contact 1 when the Organization has no Primary Contact yet.

recordUpdates.label: Account Primary Contact

recordUpdates.description: Writes Contact 1's Household onto the submission at once, so the Account rule that runs next updates that Household instead of creating a second Account, and Contact 2 and repeater rows join it.
recordUpdates.name: Update_Form_Submission_Household
recordUpdates.label: Assign the Household
